q: How do I install Revolution on Arch or CachyOS?
a: Arch / CachyOS: build `packaging/linux/arch/PKGBUILD` with `makepkg -si` (Debian / Ubuntu / Fedora use the release's .deb / .rpm). The Flatpak (`flatpak install --user <file>`) logs to `~/.var/app/ai.storyteller.filmcraft/.local/state/filmcraft/Logs/` only, not the journal; the tarball / AppImage runs unpacked with nothing system-wide.

q: Where do Flatpak logs go?

q: Where are Revolution's settings stored on Linux?
a: Revolution follows the XDG folders: your data (auto-save, recovery, presets, shortcuts, templates, models, settings) in `~/.local/share/filmcraft`; the media cache in `~/.cache/filmcraft/Media Cache` (safe to delete); logs in `~/.local/state/filmcraft/Logs`; the window size in `~/.local/state/filmcraft/window.json`. Older installs' logs and cache are moved there at first start.

q: Does Revolution remember its window size?
a: Yes: resize or maximise and quit; the next start opens at that size, maximised again if it was. Only size and maximised state are kept, not position (on Wayland the compositor places windows; KWin's Window Rules can pin it). Agents (`--control`) always start at the default size.

q: How does the Project Manager behave in full screen?
a: It remembers its own state: by default it floats in a window while the editor stays full screen, so opening a project brings it up full screen. Switch either with the full-screen button or F11 while it's showing, or in Settings ▸ General (Full screen, Project Manager full screen). Its × goes back to the open project.

q: How do I keep the menu inside the window?
a: Settings ▸ General ▸ Menu bar ▸ In the window keeps the menu in the window and nothing in the panel. The default puts it in Plasma's Global Menu when that widget is present (KDE Plasma on Wayland); elsewhere the menu stays in the window.

q: What does Revolution use the accent colour for?
a: With Use the system accent color on, the desktop's accent becomes Revolution's highlight: selections, primary buttons, the focus outline, the playhead, timecodes and track targeting. Off (default) keeps the Premiere themes' blue, the Resolve theme's red-orange or your Highlight Color. Agents use `appearance.followSystemAccent`.

q: What are the Animations options?
a: Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Animations: Sync with system (default; off when the desktop asks for reduced motion, e.g. Plasma's Animation speed at Instant or GNOME's Reduce Animation), On (always animate), Off (never). Agents use `appearance.motion` (`system`, `on`, `off`).

q: Does Ctrl+= zoom still work with Match the desktop's text size?
a: Yes, Ctrl+− / Ctrl+= still zoom for the session; a change of the desktop's text size or display scale replaces that zoom. The factor is held between 75 % and 200 %; a fixed UI Scale ignores the switch. Agents use `appearance.matchDesktopTextSize`.

q: Does export progress show on GNOME's dock?
a: Progress shows on Revolution's taskbar entry where the dock reads the Unity LauncherEntry signal (KDE Plasma's task manager; GNOME only with a dock extension). A desktop without these services shows nothing and Revolution works the same; agent sessions leave them off unless `FILMCRAFT_DESKTOP_INTEGRATION=1`.

q: Why doesn't my screen lock while Revolution plays?
a: While the Program monitor plays, Revolution asks the desktop not to blank or lock the screen, and while a job runs not to suspend, through the desktop portal (works in Flatpak) or the older ScreenSaver interface. The request is dropped when playback stops or the job ends.

q: What happens if I double-click a project while Revolution is open?
a: The running Revolution opens it (or imports the media) and its taskbar entry asks for attention; click it to bring the window forward (Wayland doesn't let apps jump in front). Each data folder has its own one-at-a-time rule, so a `--data-dir` launcher and a packaged install can run side by side.

q: Which file dialog does Revolution use on Linux?
a: Open, Import, Save and Export use the desktop's own dialog through the XDG portal (KDE's on Plasma, GNOME's on GNOME), with your Places and bookmarks. The dialog belongs to the Revolution window. File ▸ Save As of a saved project starts in the project's folder; other dialogs start where that kind was last used.

q: Where does Save As start?
a: Open, Import, Save and Export use the desktop's own dialog through the XDG portal (KDE's on Plasma, GNOME's on GNOME), with your Places and bookmarks. The dialog belongs to the Revolution window. File ▸ Save As of a saved project starts in the project's folder; other dialogs start where that kind was last used.

q: Does DRI_PRIME work with Revolution?
a: Auto follows system-wide switches: `DRI_PRIME=1` (a launcher's Run on discrete graphics), `MESA_VK_DEVICE_SELECT` or `WGPU_POWER_PREF=low`. Revolution stores a chosen GPU by its PCI ids, so driver updates don't change it, and VA-API decoding follows the choice when that GPU has a video engine. `graphics.listDevices` lists the GPUs, the stored choice and the one drawing now.

q: What happens when the sound runs dry during playback?
a: Revolution plays a moment of silence, keeps sound in step with the picture, and then mixes a little further ahead (up to half a second) for the rest of that play; a fader change is heard that much later. `perf.stats` reports `playback.audio`: callbacks, underruns, missing frames, `leadMs`, `mixerPanics`, `mixerStopped`.

q: Can I paste an image from my browser into the project?
a: On KDE Plasma (and wlroots desktops) Revolution reads the Wayland clipboard directly, so Ctrl+V of files copied in Dolphin or an image from a browser works; on GNOME it reads the clipboard through XWayland. On a touchpad two-finger scrolling moves tracks and a sideways swipe scrolls the timeline in time.

q: Do Revolution projects show in Recent Files?
a: Opening or saving a project adds it to the desktop's recent-files list (Dolphin's Recent Files, the Plasma launcher, GNOME's Recent). `.fcproj` files get their own type and double-click opens Revolution; Open With Revolution is offered for MP4, MOV, MKV, WebM, MXF, MPEG-TS, AVI, MPEG and 3GP. `filmcraft-cli thumbnail <file> <size> <out.png>` draws thumbnails.

q: Which video files offer Open With Revolution?

q: What do Next and Previous do in the desktop media controls?
a: While a sequence is open Revolution is an MPRIS player named after the sequence: Play / Pause toggles the Program monitor, Stop stops, Next / Previous step one frame, and the seek bar sets the playhead. With no sequence open there's no player.

q: Where do I change Revolution's global shortcut keys?
a: In Plasma's System Settings ▸ Keyboard ▸ Shortcuts (Revolution under Applications) or GNOME's Settings ▸ Apps ▸ Revolution. The two shortcuts are Play/Stop and Add Marker; turning Settings ▸ Playback ▸ Global shortcuts off frees the keys at once.

q: Where does a file sent with KDE Connect land on the phone?
a: It lands in the phone's Downloads folder, with KDE Connect showing the transfer. Revolution never talks to the phone directly; it asks the KDE Connect already running. Scripts: `kdeconnect.devices` lists reachable devices, `kdeconnect.send` takes `path` (or a project `item`) and `device`.

q: How does an agent send a file to the phone?

q: Does the phone's volume slider change Revolution's volume?
a: No: Revolution's own mixer and your system volume decide what you hear. Through KDE Connect's Multimedia control, play / pause, the skip buttons (one frame) and the seek bar act on the Program playhead.

q: Where are crash logs saved?
a: Logs are in `~/.local/state/filmcraft/Logs/`: filmcraft.log plus the two previous runs (filmcraft.1.log, filmcraft.2.log), and crash logs as `crash-<day>.log`. Help ▸ Reveal Log Files opens the folder. In Flatpak only the log file is written.
